subject: math
cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions

items.prompt:
Three pairs of equal sides prove congruence by:
A) AAA
B) SSS
C) SSA
D) ASA

Two sides and the included angle prove congruence by:
A) SAS
B) ASA
C) AAS
D) SSS

Which is NOT a valid congruence criterion?
A) SSS
B) SAS
C) AAA
D) ASA

Two angles and the side between them give:
A) AAS
B) ASA
C) SSA
D) SSS

Two angles and a non-included side give:
A) ASA
B) AAS
C) SAS
D) SSA

Why is AAA not a congruence criterion?
A) It uses too many parts
B) Equal angles fix shape but not size
C) It is the same as SSS
D) Angles cannot be equal
items.answer: B) Equal angles fix shape but not size

items.prompt:
SSA is called the ambiguous case because:
A) It always works
B) It can produce two different triangles
C) It needs no angles
D) It is the same as SAS
items.answer: B) It can produce two different triangles

steps: Two sides and a non-included angle can give two triangles.

items.prompt:
Triangles with angles $50°,60°$ and the included side $8$ equal are congruent by:
A) SSS
B) SAS
C) ASA
D) AAA

steps: Two angles with the included side is ASA.
